BARBELL_SQUAT.name: Squat
BARBELL_SQUAT.description: The Squat is the king of all exercises. Squats work the whole body: Your legs bend and straighten to move the weight; your abs and lower back muscles stabilize your trunk while your legs move; your upper back, shoulders and arms balance the bar on your back
goodForm: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out about 30°
Big breath and brace your abs before every rep
Push your knees out in line with your toes
Sit down until your hip crease is below the top of your knees
Keep the bar over the middle of your foot
Drive your hips up and keep your chest up
badForm: Let your knees cave inward
Lift your heels off the floor
Stop above parallel
Round or over-arch your lower back
Let the bar drift forward over your toes

DEADLIFT.name: Deadlift
DEADLIFT.description: The “dead” in Deadlift stands for dead weight. So every rep must start on the floor, from a dead stop. You don’t Deadlift top-down like on the Squat or Bench Press. You start at the bottom, pull the weight up and then return it to the floor
goodForm: Bar over the middle of your foot, shins a few centimetres away
Grip just outside your legs, arms straight
Bend your knees until your shins touch the bar
Lift your chest to flatten your back, then breathe and brace
Drag the bar up your legs
Finish standing tall with hips and knees locked
badForm: Let your hips shoot up before the bar moves
Round your lower back
Let the bar drift away from your legs
Lean back or shrug at the top
Bounce the bar off the floor between reps
Jerk the bar off the floor

BENCH_PRESS.name: Bench press
BENCH_PRESS.description: Bench-press is a full body compound exercise that works your chest, shoulders and triceps. The bench press is the most effective exercise for upper-body strength.
goodForm: Lie with your eyes under the bar
Grip a bit wider than shoulders, thumbs around the bar
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, feet planted
Lower to your lower chest with forearms vertical
Touch your chest on every rep
Press back up over your shoulders to straight arms
badForm: Use a thumbless grip
Flare your elbows straight out to the sides
Bounce the bar off your chest
Lift your hips off the bench
Let your wrists bend far back

MILITARY_PRESS.name: Overhead press
MILITARY_PRESS.description: The Overhead Press is a full body, compound exercise. Your shoulders and arms press the weight over your head while your legs, lower back and abs balance you. The Overhead Press is one of the best exercises to build strong, muscular and healthy shoulders with bigger arms.
goodForm: Grip just outside your shoulders, bar in the heel of your palm
Elbows slightly in front of the bar
Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs
Move your face back and press the bar straight up
Lock your elbows with the bar over your mid-foot
Shrug up into the bar at the top
badForm: Bend your knees to drive the bar (that is a push press)
Lean back excessively
Let your wrists fold backwards
Press the bar forward around your face
Start with your elbows behind the bar

CHINUPS.name: Chin-up
CHINUPS.description: Pullups (and chin-ups) are hard because you have to lift your entire body weight on day one. If you can't do one chin-up, do negatives: Climb up to the top position, and lift yourself down. Everybody is stronger on the way down, so you can do this. When you can do 10 good form negatives, you can do one chin-up.
goodForm: Grip with palms facing you, about shoulder-width
Start each rep from a dead hang, arms straight
Pull your elbows down toward your ribs
Get your chin over the bar
Lower under control back to straight arms
badForm: Kip or swing your legs
Do half reps
Drop into the bottom uncontrolled
Crane your neck to reach the bar

CURLS.name: Barbell curl
goodForm: Stand tall, underhand grip at shoulder width
Keep your elbows pinned at your sides
Curl until your forearms are vertical
Lower under control to straight arms
badForm: Swing the bar with your hips or back
Let your elbows drift forward
Lean back to finish the rep
Cut the bottom of the movement short

CRUNCHES.name: Weighted crunches
goodForm: Lie with knees bent and feet flat
Hold the weight against your chest
Curl your ribs toward your pelvis, lifting your shoulder blades
Breathe out on the way up
Lower slowly
badForm: Pull on your neck
Sit all the way up using your hip flexors
Use momentum
Hold your breath

BENT_OVER_ROW.name: Barbell row
BENT_OVER_ROW.description: Barbell Rows are a full body, compound exercise. They work your upper-back, lower back, hips and arms. They build a stronger, muscular back and bigger biceps. Barbell Rows are one of the most effective assistance exercises you can do to increase your Squat, Bench Press and Deadlift.
goodForm: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot, deadlift-width grip
Hinge forward with a flat back, torso near parallel to the floor
Pull the bar to your upper belly, elbows leading
Lower the bar under control each rep
badForm: Stand up as you pull
Round your back
Jerk the weight with your legs
Shorten the range of motion

DIPS.name: Dips
DIPS.description: Dips are a compound, body-weight exercise. You do Dips by first raising yourself on two dip bars with straight arms. Lower your body until your shoulders are below your elbows. Push yourself up until your arms are straight again. Dips work your chest, shoulders, back and arm muscles.
goodForm: Start at the top with elbows locked
Lean slightly forward, shoulders down and back
Lower until your shoulders are just below your elbows
Keep your elbows tracking back
Press back up to full lockout
badForm: Shrug your shoulders toward your ears
Flare your elbows wide
Bounce at the bottom
Go deeper than your shoulders tolerate
Swing your legs
